claim: On conserved fuse/split tasks, GDk9 ImplicationEngine finds a valid proof within small depth and rejects energy-mismatched targets that naive name-join/split accepts.
falsifier: Any of: a returned step with conserved=false or |delta|>1e-9; miss of conserved A,B→AB or AB→A,B within max_depth=2; kernel accepting a documented energy-mismatched target as a conserved proof; fuse→split→fuse chain breaking conservation.
assumptions: Only existing KernelPrinciple.default() maths — no new energy law
Beat is proof validity under conservation, not speed or SOTA
Naive baseline is name-only BFS join/split (intentionally weak)
